## Data Collection Methods

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### In-Person Surveys

- [In-Person Survey Guidelines](in-person-surveys.qmd)

In-person surveys remain the gold standard for detailed data collection. Through
face-to-face interviews, enumerators can build rapport with respondents, observe
behavioral cues, and collect complex information that may be difficult to obtain
through other methods.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Phone Surveys

- [Phone Survey Guidelines](phone-surveys.qmd)

Phone surveys are a cornerstone of data collection at IPA. Voice and text-based
phone surveys offer a cost-effective and adaptive method to gather high-quality
data, especially in contexts where in-person surveys are impractical.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### WhatsApp Data Collection

- [WhatsApp Surveys Guidelines](whatsapp/index.qmd)

WhatsApp has become a powerful tool for data collection, offering a
cost-effective, scalable, and user-friendly alternative to traditional survey
methods.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Administrative Data

- [Admin Data Guidelines](admin-data.qmd)

This resource provides a quick guide on obtaining and using nonpublic
administrative data for randomized evaluations.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Qualitative Methods

- [Qualitative Methods Guidelines](qualitative-methods/index.qmd)

Qualitative research methods provide invaluable insights into human experiences,
behaviors, and systems that drive change. These approaches help bridge the gap
between quantitative data and the realities of individuals and communities
participating in research studies.
:::

## Fieldwork Management

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Field Staff Training

- [Field Staff Training](fieldwork-management/field-staff-training.qmd)

Field staff training is essential to ensure safe, consistent, and high-quality
data collection. A strong training program builds enumerators' practical
interviewing skills, reinforces ethical and safety standards, and prepares teams
to handle real-world challenges across in-person and phone surveys.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Community Entry and Local Leader Engagement

- [Community Entry and Local Leader
  Engagement](fieldwork-management/community-entry-local-leaders.qmd)

Successful fieldwork depends on building trust with the communities and local
authorities who facilitate access to respondents. This guide covers how to
prepare for and conduct community entry meetings, manage relationships with
local leaders throughout data collection, and close the research team's presence
through a structured community exit.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Managing Surveyor Performance

- [Managing Surveyor
  Performance](fieldwork-management/managing-surveyor-performance.qmd)

Surveyor productivity directly affects survey budgets, timelines, and data
quality. This guide covers how to set productivity targets and monitoring
schedules before data collection begins, manage sample assignments, handle
refusals and non-response, and maintain team motivation and accountability
throughout fieldwork.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Paper Survey Data Entry

- [Paper Survey Data Entry](fieldwork-management/paper-survey-data-entry.qmd)

When data is collected on paper, digitizing it accurately requires a structured
pipeline. This guide covers how to decide between in-house and outsourced data
entry, set up and run the entry operation, reconcile discrepancies through
double entry, and verify accuracy through auditing.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Survey and Respondent Tracking

- [Survey and Respondent
  Tracking](fieldwork-management/tracking/why-tracking.qmd)

Tracking systems are essential for maintaining sample integrity and ensuring
that all participants are contacted and interviewed as planned. This section
covers survey tracking, respondent tracking, longitudinal strategies,
replacement procedures, and mop-up operations.
:::
